title: Clinical Desk Q&A: The Customer's CGM Program Status and the Strips Counted for a Day of Use
content:
The strips counted for a day of use of a Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program customer's test strips change with the status of the customer's Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program and with recent sensor refills on it.

**Rule.** 2.0 strips are added to the strips counted for every day of use when the customer's CGM program is on hold, because fingersticks then stand in for the sensor readings; 2.5 strips are taken off the strips counted for every day of use when the customer's CGM program is active and a sensor refill shipped to the customer on any of the customer's CGM programs within the last 3 calendar months, a sensor refill falling in that span when its ship date is later than the same calendar day 3 months earlier; otherwise the strips counted for a day of use are left as they are.

**Q. Which comes first when both could be read?** The on-hold addition is read first; the reduction applies only to an active CGM program.

**Q. Does an active CGM program alone take strips off?** No. It also needs a sensor refill shipped within the last 3 calendar months; an active CGM program without one leaves the strips counted as they are.

**Q. Where is the 3-month span counted to?** To today. Hypothetical: today is 15 August. A sensor refill shipped 16 May falls in the span; one shipped 15 May does not, because its ship date is not later than 15 May.

**Worked figures (hypothetical strips counted for a day of use)**

| Before this rule | CGM program | Sensor refill in the last 3 months | After this rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.0 | on hold | — | 7.0 |
| 5.0 | active | yes | 2.5 |
| 5.0 | active | no | 5.0 |
| 3.0 | active | yes | 0.5 |
| 1.5 | closed, or none held | — | 1.5 |
